correctness.rationale: PASS: From amplitude/phase equations, the active-support Jacobian is [[0,-4 diag(sigma_j chi_j I_j)],[-V_S,-kappa I]], with characteristic det[lambda(lambda+kappa)I-4DV_S]. For V_S PSD, 4DV_S has the same characteristic polynomial as real symmetric 4 sqrt(V_S) D sqrt(V_S), including singular PSD, so mu is real. Nonzero lambda=i omega would give mu=-omega²+i kappa omega nonreal: impossible for any mixed phase signs and common kappa>0. For symmetric a,b>0 dimer b<=a is PSD. For every b>a, the constructive branch with epsilon=(b-a)/(2b), I_e=I(1-epsilon), I_o=I(1+epsilon) yields t<0,d>0 and a Routh-Hurwitz threshold kappa_c²=2 b chi I (3b+5a)/a, omega²=2a chi I(b-a)/b. Independent SymPy factored t²-2kappa_c² t-4d identically to zero and confirmed threshold, as well as supplied exact witness. The crossing is transverse, not a nonlinear cycle existence theorem.

value.rationale: PASS: A uniform spectral-signature obstruction for every dimension and every active support is a structural bifurcation boundary, with a sharp converse that gives explicit physically admissible stationary parameter paths. It distinguishes indefinite nonlinear interactions from merely strongly driven PSD networks; not a routine numerical threshold for one example. It is restricted to internal spectral crossing under equal positive damping and says nothing by itself about nonlinear Hopf normal forms or dormant-mode instabilities.

limitations: Equal damping only, finite-frequency internal spectral Hopf; no inference about nonlinear periodic orbits or dormant modes.
